seo.description: About Zach Benalayat. Data Analyst, BI Developer, and Data Engineer. SQL, Python, dbt, Power BI, and Snowflake. Experience across B2B SaaS, IoT/Telecom, AI platforms, and operations.
seo.ogDescription: Data Analyst, BI Developer, and Data Engineer. 6+ years across B2B SaaS, IoT, and AI. SQL, Python, dbt, Power BI, and Snowflake.

header.heading: Hi, I'm Zach.
header.subtitle: SQL · Python · dbt · Power BI · Snowflake · Data Modeling · Forecasting

bio: I lead with the data. SQL on Snowflake, ETL/ELT and dbt models when the transforms get heavy, funnels and dashboards in Power BI / Looker / Tableau, plus A/B tests and forecasting.
I anchor every analysis to the metric that actually matters. The pipelines, semantic models, and recommendations fall out of what the data says.

points: Defined analytics frameworks and KPIs measuring API adoption, engagement, and conversion across customer touchpoints.
Behavioral funnel analysis across search, discovery, and purchase. Surfaced UX changes that reduced search time by 25%.
Designed Power BI / Looker semantic models and dashboards for exec leadership, Sales, and RevOps to monitor product performance and customer behavior.
Spearheaded identity resolution overhaul: +10% contact coverage vs LinkedIn company-contact baseline, +25% confidence in email and phone records, delivered in 3 months.

Owned the data and analytics behind the 0→1 customer-facing B2B Public API ($1M booked ARR year one), including the credit-consumption and ARR run-rate forecast. Automated analytics workflows with Claude + N8N, cutting cycle time by 15%.

SQL + Python analysis of customer, sales, and federal contracting datasets. Recommended a microtargeting shift that sales leadership adopted, driving $1M+ in enterprise contract uplift in the first re-targeting cycle.
Built Power BI semantic models tracking adoption, engagement, and bundling performance on US Navy contracts.
Ran market and competitive data analysis to support positioning and carrier partnerships.
Translated business and data insights into technical data requirements (DCMA 14-Point compliant).
Built SQL stored procedures, database tables, and ETL pipelines supporting analytics and reporting workflows for nonprofit and government clients.
Developed scalable software configurations that accelerated implementation timelines.
Partnered with customer success teams to define functional and analytics requirements.

experience.company: Latin Hyper-Texts, Butler School of Music
points: Designed and implemented the relational database architecture supporting 200K+ digitized manuscripts and large-scale research datasets.
Structured metadata frameworks enabling efficient data retrieval, analysis, and digital archiving.
Analyzed Qualtrics training and user data to improve docs and onboarding. Reduced required training sessions by 33%.

items.title: A moment that stuck
items.quote: The first time a dashboard I built talked a sales VP out of a bad call, I realized I didn't need to write another deck for that kind of meeting. He looked at the funnel for thirty seconds and changed his mind himself. The numbers do the arguing now.

items.title: Unpopular opinion
items.quote: Most dashboards are decoration. If nobody can name the decision that changes when a number moves, you've built a wall poster, not an analytics product.

items.title: Rule of thumb
items.quote: Name the metric. Model it cleanly. Check Monday.

items.title: A question I ask early
items.quote: What decision changes when this number moves? If there isn't one, we're not building a dashboard — we're building decoration.

process.heading: How I work a problem
steps: Pin down what we're actually trying to move.
Get the data, get the context, talk to whoever's closest to the problem.
Frame the KPI tree, model the data, and instrument it.
Ship the smallest thing that proves or kills the answer.
Measure honestly. Roll forward or roll back.
